allow_large: The owner asked to move every Forge install to PyPI after GitHub disabled the old repo; the nine files are the install strings, the two install scripts, the plugin marketplace and the package metadata.
done_when: Every install, upgrade, hook fallback and pinned-release command Forge prints or generates uses symphony-forge==<version> from PyPI and no command names the knacklabs GitHub repo, the plugin marketplace points at vrknetha/symphony-forge, and the package metadata carries the README and the project links so the PyPI page shows them.

findings.body: The documented install and both platform installers still pin 1.2.48. [PyPI reports](https://pypi.org/pypi/symphony-forge/json) that this version was uploaded before this patch, and the v1.2.48 source still generates installs from the disabled GitHub repository. A new user following these instructions therefore receives the old Forge, which generates broken client CI and hook fallbacks. Publishing a fixed release alone will not change these hard-coded pins; update them to that release as part of the rollout.
findings.title: Point bootstrap installs at a release containing the fix

findings.body: An existing work branch can still pin the published v1.2.48 after its default branch upgrades. This runner starts v1.2.48 from PyPI, but that release's `close` can merge the upgraded default and then its own `repo.resume_pin` invokes the new pin through the disabled GitHub URL. Closing consequently fails during the handoff, even though both versions are available from PyPI; a retry is needed after the branch pin has changed. The earlier-release test fixture copies the current source and only changes its version, so it does not exercise the historical runner.
findings.title: Handle handoff from a published legacy release

findings.body: The recovery instructions force-reinstall the shared Forge tool before checking for active work. If another build, review or CI wait is running on the machine, this can replace modules under that process and cause it to fail or mix releases. The subsequent `forge upgrade` does not provide the advertised safeguard: `upgrade.py:101–103` checks active runs only when the requested version is not already on PATH, and this command has just installed it. Have users end active runs before the forced install.
findings.title: Wait for active Forge runs before the recovery install

why: GitHub disabled the knacklabs repo, so every Forge install and upgrade line that points at git+https://github.com/knacklabs/symphony-forge@<version> fails in client CI, hooks and the pinned-release runner; Forge is now published on PyPI as symphony-forge, and its PyPI page shows no description.
